\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Inner product one set modulo two]
\lean{FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p151-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p164-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p197-b011
}
\label{FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit}
For a nonnegative integer $m$, define the subset of the $(2m)$-dimensional cube over
$\mathbb{F}_2$ consisting of all $z$ for which the inner product modulo two of the
coordinates of $z$ equals $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonempty support of the inner product]
\lean{FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet_nonempty}
\label{FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet_nonempty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit_joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet, FABL.joinF₂CubeBlocks}
\difficulty{3}
For every positive natural number $m$, there is a vector $z\in\mathbb{F}_2^{2m}$ whose
two consecutive blocks of length $m$ have inner product modulo two equal to $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Density supported on inner product one]
\lean{FABL.innerProductModTwoSupportDensity}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p144-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p164-b004
}
\label{FABL.innerProductModTwoSupportDensity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProbabilityDensity, FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet, FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet_nonempty, FABL.subsetDensity}
For a positive integer $m$, define a probability density on the $(2m)$-dimensional cube
over $\mathbb{F}_2$ by taking the uniform density on the set where the inner product
modulo two equals $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean embedding of a mod-two inner product]
\lean{FABL.booleanRealEmbedding_innerProductModTwoBit}
\label{FABL.booleanRealEmbedding_innerProductModTwoBit}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.f₂_eq_zero_or_one, FABL.innerProductModTwo, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit, FABL.realSignEncodedFunction, FABL.signEncodedFunction}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $m$ and every pair of vectors $x,y\in(\mathbb F_2)^m$,
concatenate them to form $z=(x,y)\in(\mathbb F_2)^{2m}$. The real embedding of the
mod-two inner product of the two blocks is $\bigl(1-(-1)^{\langle x,y\rangle}\bigr)/2$,
where the inner product is computed in $\mathbb F_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of the binary inner product sign]
\lean{FABL.expect_innerProductModTwo}
\label{FABL.expect_innerProductModTwo}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.innerProductModTwo, FABL.joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_innerProductModTwo_joinF₂CubeBlocks}
\difficulty{4}
For every $m\in\mathbb N$, the uniform expectation over pairs $(u,v)\in\mathbb
F_2^m\times\mathbb F_2^m$ of $(-1)^{u\cdot v}$ is $2^{-m}$, where the dot product is
computed modulo two.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of the mod-two inner-product bit]
\lean{FABL.expect_booleanRealEmbedding_innerProductModTwoBit}
\label{FABL.expect_booleanRealEmbedding_innerProductModTwoBit}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.booleanRealEmbedding_innerProductModTwoBit, FABL.expect_innerProductModTwo, FABL.innerProductModTwo, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit}
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $m$, choose uniformly a vector $z\in\mathbb{F}_2^{2m}$ and
split it into two blocks $u,v\in\mathbb{F}_2^m$. The average of the indicator that the
dot product $u\cdot v$ is $1$ in $\mathbb{F}_2$ is $\frac{1-2^{-m}}{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parity of a uniform binary inner product]
\lean{FABL.uniformProbability_innerProductModTwoOneSet}
\label{FABL.uniformProbability_innerProductModTwoOneSet}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.expect_booleanRealEmbedding_innerProductModTwoBit, FABL.f₂_eq_zero_or_one, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit, FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, choose $u,v$ independently and uniformly from
$\mathbb{F}_2^m$. The probability that their dot product in $\mathbb{F}_2$ equals $1$ is
$\frac{1-2^{-m}}{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Indicator of the inner-product-one set]
\lean{FABL.setIndicator_innerProductModTwoOneSet}
\label{FABL.setIndicator_innerProductModTwoOneSet}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.f₂_eq_zero_or_one, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit, FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet, FABL.setIndicator}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $m$, identify a vector $z\in(\mathbf F_2)^{2m}$ with a pair
$(u,v)$ of vectors in $(\mathbf F_2)^m$, and let $u\cdot v$ be their dot product over
$\mathbf F_2$. The indicator function of the set of such $z$ for which $u\cdot v=1$ is
the real-valued function that takes value $1$ when $u\cdot v=1$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise formula for the support density]
\lean{FABL.innerProductModTwoSupportDensity_apply}
\label{FABL.innerProductModTwoSupportDensity_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.booleanRealEmbedding, FABL.innerProductModTwoBit, FABL.innerProductModTwoOneSet, FABL.innerProductModTwoSupportDensity, FABL.setIndicator_innerProductModTwoOneSet, FABL.subsetDensityValue, FABL.subsetDensity_apply, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m$ be a positive natural number and let $z\in\mathbb{F}_2^{2m}$. The support
density at $z$ equals the reciprocal of the uniform probability that a vector in
$\mathbb{F}_2^{2m}$ has inner product modulo two equal to $1$, multiplied by the
indicator of that condition at $z$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier bias criterion for the support density]
\lean{FABL.innerProductModTwoSupportDensity_isBiased_iff}
\label{FABL.innerProductModTwoSupportDensity_isBiased_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.ProbabilityDensity.IsBiased, FABL.abs_vectorFourierCoeff_innerProductModTwoSupportDensity, FABL.innerProductModTwoSupportDensity}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m$ be a positive natural number and let $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{R}$. The support
density is $\varepsilon$-biased, meaning that every nonzero binary frequency has Fourier
coefficient of absolute value at most $\varepsilon$, if and only if $\varepsilon$ is at
least $\dfrac{2^{-m}}{1-2^{-m}}$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.innerProductModTwoSupportDensity_expectation}

\leanok

\difficulty{5}
For every positive natural number $m$, the expectation under the support density of the

equal to $1$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}
